todo_line: - [ ] 006 Add and focused-test the signed-in read-only targeted-add route with same-club person/group resolution, current display authority, sign-in return, protected-detail denial, heading focus, selected-person and already-member states, and scanner-safe GET behaviour that performs no membership mutation.
outcome: The existing read-only targeted-add route authorizes the current actor from Club aggregate state before resolving or rendering the target, denies actors whose club membership or management authority has been committed away even while projections lag, and labels the panel with the authoritative resolver's group name.
scope: Retain the task-006 candidate route and read-only Members-page presentation, but replace its targeted-route reliance on projected `can_add_custom_group_members?` with a narrow public Membership query backed by the Club aggregate. Its decision must match `Memba.Membership.Club` admission authority: the actor must be an active club member and either currently participate in the selected custom group or currently hold `club.manage_members` through authoritative Club role state.

Run the aggregate-backed actor check for `:targeted_add` before calling `Membership.resolve_custom_group_target_authoritatively/3` or assigning the target. Keep the host-selected club ID and the signed-in actor's resolved person ID as inputs; a false/invalid/missing result must use the existing generic denial path and must not render target details or the private member surface.

Preserve the existing authoritative target resolver call after actor authorization. Carry its `group` summary into `targeted_group_member` and render the targeted panel heading, already-member status, and consequence copy from the resolver-returned group name instead of `@selected_group.name` from the projection-backed dashboard surface.

Add focused stale-projection regressions. With the relevant Membership and/or Role projectors deliberately stopped, prove a committed actor club departure and a committed Admin-role revocation both deny the targeted GET even though projected membership/permission rows still appear active. Assert generic denial and absence of the target name/identity and existing member names; safely restart and synchronize projectors using established test helpers.

Focused-test the narrow aggregate-backed actor query itself for current custom-group participation, current Admin/manage-members authority, inactive/departed actors, revoked authority, ordinary outsiders, invalid IDs, missing/cross-club groups, and built-in-group rejection as appropriate to its public contract. Keep the existing participant, outside-admin, already-member, sign-in-return, invalid-target, focus, privacy, and scanner-safe GET coverage passing.
scope_exclusions: Do not replace or discard the existing task-006 candidate wholesale. Limit production changes to the authoritative actor boundary, propagation of resolver-owned group facts, and any minimal supporting public Membership API.

Do not dispatch `Membership.add_custom_group_member/2`, add the target, send a welcome, or add a functioning targeted Add event. Confirmation-time mutation, idempotence, and welcome behavior remain task 007.
Do not implement targeted Cancel/Escape handling, return focus, success announcements, or post-add row focus; those transitions remain task 007.

Do not broaden the ordinary dashboard's projected presentation policy beyond what is required to secure the targeted route. Do not expose the Club aggregate itself or query Ecto schemas directly from the LiveView.
Do not alter request-access messaging/UI, email rendering, route shape, general custom-group picker/removal behavior, accepted feature files, or the iteration-066 browser journey.

Do not edit the approved plan, ADRs, iteration acceptance criteria, or project reference docs. Do not run `dev check`, `dev check --quick`, `dev ci`, or another unscoped full-suite command in this revision.

references.facts: The candidate currently gates `:targeted_add` on projected `can_add_custom_group_members?`, then calls the accepted target resolver; `present_targeted_group_member/1` discards `target.group`. Revise this seam so aggregate-backed actor authority precedes target resolution and the resolver-owned group summary reaches presentation.

This ordinary dashboard loader combines authoritative group-participation summaries with projected active membership and `MemberPermission` authorization. It may continue shaping the normal surface, but its `can_add_custom_group_members?` value is not sufficient for the privacy-sensitive targeted route when Membership or Role projections lag.

Membership already centralizes narrow public aggregate-backed reads and typed-ID error handling. Add the smallest public actor-authority query here, returning no aggregate/projection schema, and reuse the existing private helpers where practical.

The existing private aggregate decision is the semantic authority to mirror: an active actor membership may manage a custom group through current participation or a current aggregate-held `club.manage_members` grant. Keep the public read aligned with this rule rather than narrowing authority to the built-in Admin label or trusting flattened projections.
These functions read `MemberPermission` projections and are the source of the stale-authority gap. They must not decide targeted-route authority after a committed revocation or departure.

The candidate currently passes projected `@selected_group.name`. Pass the resolver-owned targeted group name instead while preserving the established Members-page placement and outside-admin conversation privacy.

The candidate component already has stable target/focus/status IDs. Preserve those semantics; only adjust its group-name input shape if needed to ensure all targeted copy comes from the authoritative target summary.

The seven candidate tests cover route display, ordinary denial, inactive actor after projections catch up, invalid targets, already-member state, focus, privacy, and inert GET. Add stale Role/Membership projection cases that demonstrate the reviewed gap, following supervised-projector stop/restart patterns already used elsewhere.

This focused file establishes accepted aggregate-read and stale-projection testing conventions. Extend it for the new narrow actor query or add a comparably focused sibling test without weakening target-resolver coverage.
Active membership and role authority are Club-owned facts; projected preflight state cannot be the final privacy-sensitive authority after a committed departure or revocation.
Current aggregate-held group participation, not stale projected state, governs a participant's access.
Keep authorization in the LiveView/domain boundary and retain selector-based tests and the candidate's route-driven state.

constraints: Use `d1d755586b5958bfad6fad7d439fed0569e9a9e9` as the revision baseline and preserve task identity 006 and candidate origin `006-8d42dd1-1`.
The host-selected club remains authoritative; never derive club context or actor authority from the URL, projected selected group, target identity, email body, referer, or client input.

The aggregate-backed read must mirror the Club command rule for current participation or current `club.manage_members` permission, including custom roles that grant that permission; do not hard-code only the Admin role name.
Deny before target resolution/assignment. A stale projected membership, permission, member list, or candidate list must not make a departed or revoked actor eligible for targeted display.

Use only `Membership.resolve_custom_group_target_authoritatively/3` output for the target person, membership, group, and current already-member facts. In particular, targeted copy must not use the projection-backed selected-group name.
Keep both disconnected GET and connected mount read-only: no membership command, group event, welcome, pending state, follow change, or conversation access change.
Generic denial evidence must omit the target name, person ID, membership ID, member-list names, group email, messages, and compose controls.
Projector-lag tests must use supervised stop/restart and deterministic synchronization such as projection barriers or `_ = :sys.get_state/1`; do not use `Process.sleep/1`.
completion_evidence_required: Return every changed path and identify the public aggregate-backed actor query, how it matches `Club.authorize_custom_group_admission_actor/3`, and where `MemberDashboardLive` invokes it before target resolution.

Show focused tests where projected membership/permission data remains stale after a committed actor departure and after a committed management-role revocation, yet each targeted GET receives generic denial with no target or member-list details.

Show both authority branches still succeed: a current custom-group participant and a current outside club member with aggregate-held `club.manage_members` authority can view the targeted Members state.
Show the targeted heading, already-member status, and consequence copy receive the group name returned by `Membership.resolve_custom_group_target_authoritatively/3`, not `@selected_group.name`.
Confirm all pre-existing task-006 cases remain passing and GET/mount still emit no group-add event or welcome email.
Confirm no targeted admission event, welcome dispatch, Cancel/Escape behavior, success transition, acceptance-feature change, or browser-journey enablement was included.
Record each focused validation command, working directory, exit status, and test/failure counts; list any unresolved issue.
